sections.heading: 1. Overview
sections.body: DevToolBox ("we", "our", "us") operates zhujiuyin.com. This page explains what information we collect, how we use it, and the choices you have. By using the site you agree to this policy.

sections.heading: 2. Data you provide to the tools

sections.heading: 6. Third-party services

sections.heading: 7. Children's privacy

sections.heading: 8. Changes

json-formatter.name: JSON Formatter
json-formatter.description: Format, minify, and validate JSON with syntax highlighting.
json-formatter.page_desc: Paste your JSON to format, validate, and explore with a tree view. Data stays in your browser.
json-formatter.seo_desc: Format, beautify, minify, and validate JSON online. Free developer tool — no sign-up required.
json-formatter.placeholder: Paste JSON on the left to see results
json-formatter.faq_text: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a lightweight data interchange format widely used in web APIs and configuration files. This tool helps you format, beautify, minify, and validate JSON data in your browser. Your data stays local and is never sent to any server.
features: Real-time JSON validation with error position highlighting
Interactive tree view with collapsible nodes
Format with configurable indentation (2, 4, or 8 spaces)
Minify JSON to reduce file size
Copy formatted or minified output with one click
use_cases: Debug API responses by pretty-printing compact JSON returned from servers.
Clean up minified JSON from browser DevTools to read it more easily.
Validate that a config file parses before committing it to a repo.
Minify JSON to reduce payload size before embedding in HTML or query strings.

faq_list.q: Is my JSON data uploaded anywhere?
faq_list.a: No. Parsing, formatting, and validation happen entirely in your browser with the built-in JSON engine. The data never leaves your device.

faq_list.q: What is the difference between format and minify?
faq_list.a: Format adds whitespace and indentation for readability. Minify removes all unnecessary whitespace to produce the smallest valid JSON string.

faq_list.q: Why does my JSON fail to parse?
faq_list.a: JSON is strict: keys and strings must use double quotes, trailing commas are not allowed, and comments are not supported. The error banner shows the position of the first problem.
Yes — enable "Sort Keys" in the toolbar to sort keys alphabetically at every level of the tree.

base64.name: Base64 Encode / Decode
base64.description: Encode text to Base64 or decode Base64 back to plain text.
base64.page_desc: Encode text to Base64 or decode Base64 strings instantly.
base64.seo_desc: Encode text to Base64 or decode Base64 back to plain text. Supports Unicode and CJK characters.
base64.encode_error: Failed to encode — input may contain unsupported characters.
base64.decode_error: Failed to decode — input is not valid Base64.
base64.faq_text: Base64 is a binary-to-text encoding scheme that represents binary data as an ASCII string. It is commonly used to embed binary data in JSON, HTML, emails, and URLs. This tool supports full Unicode text including CJK characters.
use_cases: Embed small images or fonts inline in CSS or HTML using data URIs.
Encode binary payloads so they can travel safely inside JSON or XML.
Decode Basic Auth tokens (the value after "Basic " in the Authorization header).
Inspect the payload section of a JWT (the middle segment between the dots).

faq_list.q: Does Base64 encryption protect my data?
faq_list.a: No. Base64 is an encoding, not encryption — anyone can decode it. Use it for transport, not for secrecy.

faq_list.q: How much larger is Base64 output?
faq_list.a: Base64 expands binary data by roughly 33% (every 3 bytes become 4 characters).

faq_list.q: Does this tool support Chinese, Japanese, or emoji?
faq_list.a: Yes. Input is first converted to UTF-8 bytes before encoding, so all Unicode characters round-trip correctly.

faq_list.q: Why does my decoded result look garbled?
faq_list.a: The input may be URL-safe Base64 (using - and _ instead of + and /) or may contain stray whitespace. Clean the string and try again.

url-encoder.name: URL Encoder / Decoder
url-encoder.description: Encode or decode URLs and query string parameters.
url-encoder.page_desc: Encode or decode URLs and query string parameters.
url-encoder.seo_desc: Encode or decode URLs and query string parameters. Supports encodeURIComponent and encodeURI.
url-encoder.faq_text: URL encoding (percent-encoding) replaces unsafe characters with a % followed by two hex digits. encodeURIComponent encodes everything except A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ . ! ~ * ' ( ), making it ideal for query parameters. encodeURI preserves URI structure characters like : / ? # &.
use_cases: Build query strings that include spaces, symbols, or non-ASCII characters.
Decode a logged URL to see what a user actually submitted.
Safely pass a redirect target as a query parameter.
Debug issues where servers receive unexpected characters.

faq_list.q: What is the difference between encodeURI and encodeURIComponent?
faq_list.a: encodeURI preserves URI-structural characters like : / ? # &, so it is appropriate for whole URLs. encodeURIComponent encodes those characters too, so it is the right choice for a single query parameter value.

faq_list.q: Why is a space encoded as %20 sometimes and + other times?
faq_list.a: %20 is the standard percent-encoding for a space. The + form is a legacy rule specific to the application/x-www-form-urlencoded body format used by HTML forms.

faq_list.q: Do I need to encode Chinese characters?
faq_list.a: Yes. Non-ASCII characters must be UTF-8 encoded and then percent-encoded to travel through URLs reliably. This tool handles that automatically.

regex-tester.name: Regex Tester
regex-tester.description: Test regular expressions against text with real-time match highlighting.
regex-tester.page_desc: Test regular expressions with real-time match highlighting.
regex-tester.seo_desc: Test JavaScript regular expressions with real-time match highlighting and capture group display.
regex-tester.test_placeholder: Type text to test against the regex pattern...
regex-tester.faq_text: This tool lets you test JavaScript-compatible regular expressions in real time. Matches are highlighted in the test string, and capture groups are shown in the results table. Supports global (g), case-insensitive (i), multiline (m), dotAll (s), and unicode (u) flags.
use_cases: Validate email, phone, or ID formats before shipping a form validator.
Extract URLs, dates, or numbers from a block of log text.
Debug a pattern that is not matching as you expect by seeing matches highlighted live.
Prototype a replacement rule before dropping it into your code editor.

faq_list.q: Which regex dialect does this tool use?
faq_list.a: The JavaScript RegExp engine. Features like lookbehind and named captures are supported in modern browsers.

faq_list.q: Why does my pattern only match once?
faq_list.a: Without the g (global) flag, only the first match is returned. Enable g to find all matches.

faq_list.q: How do I match across newlines?
faq_list.a: Use the s flag (dotAll) to make . match newline characters, or use \s explicitly.

timestamp.name: Timestamp Converter
timestamp.description: Convert between Unix timestamps and human-readable dates.
timestamp.page_desc: Convert between Unix timestamps and human-readable dates.
timestamp.seo_desc: Convert between Unix timestamps and human-readable dates. Supports seconds, milliseconds, and ISO 8601.
timestamp.input_label: Enter a Unix timestamp or date string
timestamp.empty_error: Please enter a timestamp or date string.
timestamp.parse_error: Unable to parse input. Try a Unix timestamp or ISO 8601 date.
timestamp.faq_text: A Unix timestamp is the number of seconds since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC (the Unix Epoch). This tool converts between Unix timestamps (seconds or milliseconds) and human-readable date formats including ISO 8601, UTC, and your local timezone.
use_cases: Translate a timestamp from logs or a database into a readable date in your timezone.
Check whether a timestamp is stored in seconds or milliseconds.
Generate a timestamp for an API request that requires epoch time.
Compare two events by seeing their ISO 8601 UTC values side by side.

faq_list.q: Seconds or milliseconds — which should I use?
faq_list.a: Unix standard is seconds. JavaScript's Date.now() uses milliseconds. A 13-digit number is almost always milliseconds; a 10-digit number is seconds.
No. It is always counted from the UTC epoch. Conversion to a local clock time is done when you display it.
Signed 32-bit timestamps overflow in January 2038. Use 64-bit integers (or a language runtime that does) to stay safe.
